260	  description, background })` per crew member, dispatched as separate `Agent` calls in one
261	  message. `agentId` is the crew member's resolved `chosen.id`; the call derives its model
262	  lane from the shared manifest, so a dispatch can never contradict the installed agent
263	  file's stamped `model_preference` -- and Kimi takes a LANE (`primary`|`secondary`), never
264	  a model id.
265	
266	**The lanes ENGAGE only because the run loop binds them per-process.** A stamped
267	`model_preference` is inert until the secondary-model experiment is on for the process --
268	`kimiGoalInvocation` (the go.md step-6 Kimi run loop) sets `KIMI_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_FLAG=1`
269	+ `KIMI_SECONDARY_MODEL` from the single derivation `kimiLaneEnv()` (`src/kimi.js`), and
270	the flag is also what selects the v2 engine under `kimi -p`. The interactive TUI ignores
271	`model_preference` entirely, so lanes bind under a muster-launched `kimi -p`, never in the
272	TUI (docs/research/kimi-code-cli.md sec 11.8). `muster doctor`'s `kimi-lane-binding` check
273	reports the active binding.
274	
275	**Attended sessions dispatch lane-sensitive legs as headless `kimi -p` processes.** The
276	AgentSwarm/agent-calls shapes above are the UNATTENDED in-session path -- lanes bind there
277	only because `kimiGoalInvocation` (go.md step 6) already set the env pair for the whole run
278	loop. An ATTENDED/interactive session (a human driving this skill in the TUI) has no such
279	bind, and the TUI ignores `model_preference` entirely, so an in-session `Agent` call there
280	can never engage a lane. Lane-sensitive legs in an attended session therefore dispatch via
281	`kimiProcessDispatch({ brief, agentFile, cwd, lane })` (`src/kimi-dispatch.js`) -- one
282	headless `kimi -p` process per leg, spawned straight from the descriptor's `{ argv, env,
283	cwd, lane }`: `argv` is `["-p", brief, "--agent-file", <absolute agent file>,
284	"--output-format", "stream-json", "-m", KIMI_LANES[lane]]`, and `env` is the shared
285	`kimiLaneEnv()` OVERRIDE pair, carried for the v2 engine flag `--agent-file` needs (its
286	`KIMI_SECONDARY_MODEL` half also binds lanes for any subagents the leg itself spawns) --
287	merge it over the ambient process env at spawn (`{ ...process.env, ...d.env }`), never
288	pass it as the whole env (a wholesale replacement loses HOME/PATH and the child breaks). `-m` is ALWAYS
289	emitted, for the primary lane too: `model_preference` binds only a process's SPAWNED
290	SUBAGENTS, never the `-p` process's own main agent, so the process's model comes ONLY from
291	`-m` and omitting it silently falls to config `default_model`. The leg's receipt is the
292	stream-json result on stdout plus the process exit code, with per-leg token accounting from
293	`readSessionUsage` (`src/kimi-receipts.js`) over the fresh session dir the process writes
294	(docs/research/kimi-code-cli.md sec 8). Reserve the attended session's native `Agent` tool
295	for legs that genuinely need the parent's live context; the pre-validation, resume-retry,
296	and background rules below keep governing the unattended in-session path, which a process
297	lane never replaces mid-loop.
298	
299	**Pre-validate the four swarm rejection rules BEFORE dispatch -- never pay a whole-wave
300	round trip to learn them.** Kimi rejects a malformed swarm before any subagent starts, so
301	a bad packet costs the wave's entire fan-out. `kimiSwarmCall` enforces all four up front
302	and throws with the offending detail named: (1) at least 2 items unless resuming; (2)
303	`prompt_template` required whenever items are present; (3) the template must contain the
304	exact `{{item}}` placeholder; (4) -- absent from Kimi's published docs, enforced in the
305	binary -- the FILLED prompts must be DISTINCT: two items expanding to the same prompt
306	reject the WHOLE swarm, and duplicate wave items (two crew members handed the same file)
307	are exactly how muster would trip it. On a validation error, FIX the packet (rename or
308	merge the duplicate item, repair the template) and rebuild; a wave that cannot satisfy the
309	distinct-prompts rule is not a uniform fan-out at all -- resolve it as agent-calls instead.
310	
311	**Failure retry rides the same native shapes.** Step 4a's re-dispatch-once rule RESUMES on
312	Kimi instead of re-spawning (docs/research/kimi-code-cli.md sec 6): a failed per-agent call is
313	retried as `kimiAgentCall({ resume: <failed agent id>, prompt: <error context> })` -- Kimi's
314	`resume` is mutually exclusive with `subagent_type`, and a resumed subagent keeps its model, so
315	the retry packet drops the lane override too; a failed swarm member is retried as
316	`kimiSwarmCall({ resumeAgentIds: { <failed agent id>: <error context> } })` -- which is also why
317	the >=2-item floor lifts when resuming. One retry, the same cap every harness gets; a second
318	failure escalates exactly as step 4a says.
